en.title: Largest Three-Digit Number in Original Order
en.description:
Given n decimal digits, choose 1 to 3 of them in their original order and concatenate them into an integer; find the largest integer you can get. The chosen digits need not be contiguous; their relative order cannot change; leading zeros are allowed, and the integer is output without leading zeros.

This problem uses a standard input/output format compiled by CSWork; the algorithm rules follow the source problem, and the examples and test data were written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n (3 ≤ n ≤ 50); the second line contains n digits (0 ≤ digits[i] ≤ 9).
en.explanation: Example 1 chooses 7, 4 and 9 at indices 0, 4 and 5 to get 749; 9 cannot be moved in front of 7.
hints: best[k] stores the largest value that can be formed by choosing exactly k digits from the processed prefix. When reading digit d, update best[k]=max(best[k],best[k−1]×10+d) in reverse order so that no digit is used more than once.
